title: Letter 20 — On Slander and the Evil Tongue
attribution_note: Letter 20 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: Here, according to your request, I send you the teaching of Saint Chrysostom on the evil tongue, from which you will see how heavy and foul a vice is condemnation and slander.
So then, listen to what he says of the evil-tongued:

*“Though, condemning your neighbour, you should speak even what is true concerning him, and though you should reproach him for a deed that is known, yet even for this you shall not escape punishment; for God will judge you not according to his deeds, but according to your words.* *For He saith: 'By thy words thou shalt be condemned'”* [Matthew 12:37]. *“The Pharisee spoke what was true and known to all, yet even for this he received punishment.* *And if known deeds ought not to be spoken to the reproach of others, much less those that are doubtful.”* (Homily 42 on the Evangelist Matthew)

sections.heading: We bite and devour one another

pairs.en: *“What profit is there that we abstain from birds and fishes, when we bite and devour one another?* *For every slanderer and reviler bites and devours the flesh of his neighbour.”* (Homily on the Departure of Bishop Flavian)

*“Though we should eat ashes, even so strict a life will bring us no profit, if we do not refrain from reviling.* *For 'not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man'”* [Matthew 15:11]. (Homily on the Departure of Bishop Flavian)

*“What kind of evil does not spring from reviling?* *From it are born hatreds; from it come enmities and discords; from it arise evil suspicions, which become the cause of countless evils.”* (Homily on Psalm 100)
*“Whoever loves slander serves the devil.”* (Homily on Psalm 100)

*“As the preacher of truth by his word saves many men, so, on the contrary, the slanderer by that same word destroys a great multitude, uttering words that drown them, and employing the sword of speech for the ruin of men.* *Moreover the slanderer kills not only bodies, but the very souls themselves, when with his flattering tongue he plants in them false and lawless opinions.”* (Homily on Psalm 51)
*“One ought not only to refrain from reviling one's neighbour, but even from listening to others who revile him.”* (Homily 3 on the Departure of Bishop Flavian)

You see how the great teacher thunders against the sin of condemnation and slander. Many do not kill or wound a man with their hands, but they wound and kill with the tongue, as with a weapon, according as it is written: *“the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword”* [Psalm 56:5].

Many do not eat fish, meat, milk and other food which God has not forbidden, but has even blessed the faithful who know the truth to receive with thanksgiving (see 1 Timothy 4:3–4), yet they devour living men. Many give no scandal by their deeds — this is good and praiseworthy — but with the tongue they spread scandals, and carry evil from place to place, as one infected carries infection, and as the wind carries fire, from which many calamities and misfortunes arise. Many keep the traditions of the fathers — and this too is good — yet they destroy the commandment of God: *“Judge not,”* and *“neither accuse any falsely”* [Matthew 7:1; Luke 3:14], which is blindness and extreme folly.

All Christians pray to God, sing to God, and partake of the Body and Blood of Christ, and confess His holy and fearful name — this is the Christian's work — yet this is fearful and heavy and truly worthy of lament: that many of them defile those very mouths with condemnation, slander and evil-speaking — those mouths, I say, with which they pray, with which they sing to God, and with which they touch the Body and Blood of Christ.

Therefore take care, beloved, of your mouth, with which you confess God, sing to Him and partake of the holy Mysteries, lest you become altogether unclean and abominable before God. Think and reason that you too are such a sinner as the rest. And when you see or hear anything evil in your neighbour, seal your lips with silence, and for him sigh unto the Lord, that He may correct him; and for yourself pray, that you fall not into such a vice. For we are all subject to every fall, as being weak. *“Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall,”* the apostle exhorts. [1 Corinthians 10:12]
